(i) the interacting boson approximation is a good one for the N = 98 to 114 tungsten isotopes and (ii) the interacting bosons in this region are well described as a superposition of two nondegeneracies, the sum of which equals the number of valence nucleons.
the interacting boson approximation is a very good approximation for the tungsten and osmium isotopes, and that the interacting bosons can be identified with the quadrupole and octupole phonons.
the generalized seniority shell-model scheme provides a simple and accurate microscopic basis for the interacting bosons model.

the microscopic derivation of the interacting bosons from fermions and the determination of the interacting-boson model parameters.
the microscopic determination of the interacting-boson model (IBM) parameters.
the development of an interacting boson model which can be applied to a wide range of nuclear systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interacting boson approximation is a good one in the N = Z to 40 region, and that it becomes increasingly less good as one goes away from this region.
the interacting boson scheme is a reasonable approximation for the tungsten region.
, in general, the interacting boson approximation to the nuclear many-body problem is quite successful, and the interacting boson parameters are reasonably well determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the generalized seniority approach to the interacting boson approximation is a useful tool in the study of the interacting bosons in nondegenerate j shell configurations.

the generalized seniority model provides a microscopic basis for the interacting bosons model and that this model is a good approximation to the shell-model description in the region of the periodic table being studied.
a microscopic approach based on the generalized seniority concept provides a useful framework for the interpretation of interacting boson model results.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the interacting boson picture can be obtained by a simple mapping of the underlying fermion system in the case of two nondegenerates, and this mapping can be applied to any nucleus in the periodic table.

the interacting boson approximation is valid for the low-lying states of nuclei with nondegenerate j-shell structure provided the number of nucleons is large enough so that the number of bosons is large.
the interacting boson scheme can be used to describe a wide variety of nuclei in the periodic table.
